questions.question: Compare the medical model with the biopsychosocial model of mental illness.

points.text: Medical model: mental illness is a disease with biological causes (genetics, neurotransmitters, brain abnormalities). Treatment: medication (drugs). Biopsychosocial model: mental illness results from biological, psychological and social factors interacting. Treatment: combination of medication, therapy and social support. The biopsychosocial model is more comprehensive but harder to implement.

questions.question: Explain how cultural factors can affect the diagnosis of mental health problems.

points.text: Cultural factors: symptoms vary by culture (e.g. depression expressed as physical pain in some Asian cultures); culture-bound syndromes don't fit Western diagnoses; diagnostic criteria (DSM-5, ICD-11) are Western-developed and may not generalise; language barriers affect diagnosis; stigma varies across cultures. Result: people from minority cultures may be misdiagnosed or under-diagnosed.

questions.question: Evaluate whether the medical model is the best approach to understanding mental illness.

points.text: Medical model strengths: scientific basis (brain chemistry evidence), effective drug treatments (SSRIs for depression), reduces blame (illness not personal failure). Limitations: reductionist (ignores social and psychological causes), over-reliance on medication (side effects, doesn't address root causes), deterministic (implies individuals cannot change).
